market_context: United States and general English-speaking market
title: Hummus vs. tahini: nutrition differences

seo.title: Hummus vs. tahini: nutrition differences
seo.meta_description: Tahini is far more concentrated than hummus. Compare equal 30 g servings for calories, protein, fat, fiber and minerals.
seo.search_intent: Compare hummus and tahini nutrition using equal serving weights

excerpt: Hummus and tahini are not interchangeable foods: tahini is concentrated sesame paste and is often one ingredient in hummus. In equal 30 g servings, the USDA references used here provide about 73 calories, 2.2 g protein, 5.1 g fat and 1.6 g fiber for hummus, versus about 209 calories, 5.9 g protein, 18.7 g fat and 2.5 g fiber for tahini.
content_html:
Hummus and tahini sit next to each other so often that they can look like two versions of the same dip. They are not. Tahini is ground sesame; hummus usually combines tahini with chickpeas, water or lemon and other ingredients. That difference dramatically changes nutrient concentration.

Equal weights make the contrast clear

Per 30 gPlain hummusTahini
Calories~73~209
Protein~2.2 g~5.9 g
Fat~5.1 g~18.7 g
Fiber~1.6 g~2.5 g
Carbohydrate~4.5 g~4.3 g

Tahini has almost three times the calories at the same weight because sesame paste is much richer in fat. That is not a nutritional flaw; it means a tablespoon of tahini should not be interpreted like a tablespoon of hummus.

Why tahini provides more protein and minerals per gram

The tahini reference contains about 19.7 g protein, 357 mg magnesium and 7 mg iron per 100 g. Hummus, because the sesame is mixed with chickpeas and wetter ingredients, comes in at about 7.3 g protein per 100 g and is less mineral-dense.

Thirty grams of tahini therefore provides about 107 mg magnesium and 2.1 mg iron. Calcium is more product-dependent because sesame hull removal can change it substantially.

Hummus gives you more volume for fewer calories

A 60 g serving of hummus works out to roughly 146 calories, 4.4 g protein and 3.2 g fiber in the reference used here. Sixty grams of tahini would exceed 400 calories. In real meals, tahini is usually used in smaller quantities precisely because it is so concentrated.

Which one makes more sense?

They play different roles. Hummus can be a larger dip or spread combining legumes, sesame and plant fat. Tahini works especially well as a smaller ingredient in dressings, sauces and hummus itself.

If you want more protein or magnesium per gram, tahini wins. If you want more volume and fewer calories per spoonful, hummus generally fits better.

The useful question is not which one is healthier, but how much you are using and what job it has in the meal.

faq.question: Which has more protein, hummus or tahini?
faq.answer: Tahini by weight: about 19.7 g/100 g versus 7.3 g/100 g in the hummus reference.

faq.question: Which has more calories?
faq.answer: Tahini clearly: about 697 calories/100 g versus 243 calories/100 g in the hummus reference.

faq.question: Is tahini an ingredient in hummus?
faq.answer: Yes. Classic hummus typically combines tahini with chickpeas, lemon, garlic and other ingredients depending on the recipe.

faq.question: Which has more fiber?
faq.answer: Per 100 g, the tahini reference has 8.4 g versus 5.4 g in hummus, although tahini is usually eaten in a smaller serving.
